jobs.title: Accounting Specialist
jobs.description:
The purpose of Idorsia is to discover, develop and commercialize innovative medicines to help more patients. To achieve this, we will develop Idorsia into a leading biopharmaceutical company, with a strong scientific core.

Make an impact in a collaborative international finance team.

We're looking for a detail-oriented and proactive Accounting Specialist to join our Finance team. In this role, you'll help ensure the smooth running of our day-to-day financial operations while contributing to accurate financial reporting and the continuous digitalization and automation of finance processes, helping to improve efficiency, data quality, and the overall user experience.

Working closely with colleagues across the business, you'll play an important role in accounts payable, general accounting, month-end closing activities, and finance projects in an international environment.

Your responsibilities

• Process vendor invoices accurately and in compliance with internal policies and regulatory requirements.

• Review and process employee expense claims and payment requests.

• Prepare payment runs and perform bank postings and reconciliations.

• Maintain accounts payable subledgers and resolve posting discrepancies.

• Respond to vendor and internal stakeholder inquiries regarding invoices, payments, and account balances.

• Support month-end, quarter-end, and year-end closing activities, including audits and VAT reporting.

• Contribute to ERP enhancements and finance process improvement initiatives.

• Provide support across the Finance team on additional accounting activities as required.

What you'll bring

• Commercial apprenticeship or equivalent qualification with accounting experience.

• Further education or a degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field is an advantage.

• Fluent in English, both written and spoken; German and/or French are an asset

• At least five years of experience in a similar accounting role, ideally within an international company.

• Sound understanding of accounting principles and accounts payable processes.

• Experience working with ERP systems and Microsoft Excel.

• A structured, reliable, and detail-oriented working style with a continuous improvement mindset.

• Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to working with colleagues and external partners.

Why join us?

• Be part of an international and collaborative Finance team.

• Take ownership of diverse accounting responsibilities with real business impact.

• Help shape the digital transformation of Finance by contributing to automation and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Grow your expertise in a dynamic and supportive environment.

Work  Location: Allschwil, Switzerland

Business Area: Global Finance & Procurement

Schedule: Fulltime

Job Type: Permanent

Job ID : 4795

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about patient safety and ensuring that medicines are monitored to the highest standards? As a Drug Safety Case Manager, you will play a critical role in safeguarding patients by ensuring accurate and timely management of safety information throughout the product lifecycle.

Working within a collaborative and highly skilled Drug Safety team, you will take ownership of adverse event case management activities while partnering closely with physicians, clinical teams, regulatory colleagues, and external partners to ensure compliance with global pharmacovigilance requirements.

Your Responsibilities:

Case Management & Safety Reporting

• Manage adverse event cases from receipt through submission, including triage, data entry, medical coding, narrative writing, quality review, and expedited reporting for both clinical trial and post-marketing cases

• Prioritize and process safety cases in accordance with global regulations, SOPs, and reporting timelines

• Identify missing or incomplete information and coordinate follow-up activities with Drug Safety Physicians and other stakeholders

• Monitor case workflows to ensure efficient and compliant case processing

• Support or oversee reconciliation activities to ensure data consistency across systems

Clinical Trial & Cross-Functional Support

• Contribute to the successful set-up of new clinical studies by providing safety reporting documentation, reconciliation plans, monitoring guidance, and TMF documentation

• Support SAE reconciliation activities between clinical and safety databases

• Coordinate SUSAR notifications to investigators and Ethics Committees

• Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders, including CROs, to establish and maintain safety agreements and processes

What You'll Bring:

• Degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Nursing, or a related healthcare discipline

• Minimum 5 years of experience in drug safety case management

• Strong understanding of medical terminology, disease processes, and safety databases

• Experience with medical coding dictionaries and safety reporting systems

• Good knowledge of EU and US pharmacovigilance regulations and reporting requirements

• Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines

• Strong attention to detail, problem-solving abilities, and a collaborative mindset

• Fluent English, both written and spoken

• EU/EFTA citizenship is required due to permit restrictions

Why Join Us?

This role offers the opportunity to make a direct impact on patient safety while working in a dynamic, international environment. You will collaborate with experienced professionals across clinical development and pharmacovigilance, contribute to innovative clinical programs, and play a key role in ensuring the safe use of medicines.

About Idorsia Pharmaceuticals Ltd

Headquartered near Basel, Switzerland – a European biotech hub – Idorsia has a highly experienced team of dedicated professionals, covering all disciplines from bench to bedside; QUVIVIQ™ (daridorexant), a different kind of insomnia treatment with the potential to revolutionize this mounting public health concern; strong partners to maximize the value of our portfolio; a promising in-house development pipeline; and a specialized drug discovery engine focused on small-molecule drugs that can change the treatment paradigm for many patients.

We are looking for a  VP, Head of Global Access, Value and Pricing  to join the company!

Job Responsibilities

The VP , Head of Global Access, Value & Pricing   is responsible for defining and driving the global market access, value, and pricing strategy for priority pipeline and launch assets across their lifecycle.

The role serves as the global market access representative within cross-functional asset teams, ensuring payer requirements are embedded into product development, evidence generation, launch planning, pricing strategies, and lifecycle management to facilitate timely patient access and maximize asset value.

Working closely with Commercial, Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Regulatory, Finance, and Regional Access teams, the role translates complex payer and reimbursement requirements into actionable global strategies and enables successful local execution.

• Define and lead global market access strategies from early development through launch and lifecycle management.

• Act as the core market access representative on global asset teams and provide strategic access leadership across functions.

• Embed payer requirements into target product profiles, clinical development plans, integrated product strategies, and indication sequencing.

• Provide access input on clinical endpoints, comparators, target populations, outcomes measures, and evidence-generation plans.

• Develop payer-focused evidence roadmaps aligned with development milestones and launch objectives.

• Build robust payer value propositions tailored to key reimbursement and Health Technology Assessment (HTA) stakeholders.

• Design and execute integrated global access roadmaps covering reimbursement, affordability, pricing, and access considerations.

• Identify potential market access barriers and develop mitigation strategies based on payer insights and evolving healthcare policies.

• Lead payer research, competitive access assessments, and reimbursement landscape analyses across priority markets.

• Design innovative access solutions, including managed entry agreements, value-based arrangements, patient support programs, and affordability initiatives.

• Ensure access strategies are compliant and adaptable to regional and local healthcare systems.

• Co-lead global pricing strategy development in collaboration with cross-functional stakeholders.

• Establish and support pricing governance frameworks to optimize global and local pricing decisions.

• Assess and manage pricing risks, including international reference pricing implications and downstream market impact.

• Develop and maintain key global access deliverables, including Global Value Dossiers, payer value decks, value narratives, and reimbursement materials.

• Create global access toolkits and support regional and country teams with payer engagement, submissions, negotiations, and launch preparation.

• Partner with forecasting and finance teams to ensure access assumptions are reflected in commercial forecasts and business planning.

• Monitor healthcare policy, reimbursement, HTA, and regulatory developments and translate implications into strategic recommendations.

• Support launch readiness activities to ensure successful payer engagement and market access execution.

• Represent the global access perspective in governance discussions, asset teams, and external partnerships where appropriate.

• Drive alignment between Global, Regional, and Local teams to ensure consistent and effective access strategies across markets.

 University degree in Life Sciences, Health Economics, Economics, Business Administration, Public Health, or a related discipline.

•
 Significant experience in Market Access, Pricing, Value Strategy, or Reimbursement within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

•

 Strong understanding of healthcare systems, reimbursement pathways, payer decision-making, and Health Technology Assessment (HTA) processes across major markets.

 Experience in Health Economics and Outcomes Research (HEOR) considered a strong advantage.

 Experience contributing to economic models, value dossiers, real-world evidence strategies, and payer evidence planning desirable.
